safety_verdicts.content: Patient presents with lip swelling for the past 1 hour.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated documentation notes lip swelling after prawn exposure but does not include the duration ('past 1 hour').
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the exact duration of lip swelling (past 1 hour) slightly reduces timeline clarity but does not materially change recognition of a likely acute allergic reaction already prompting emergency escalation. This is unlikely to affect immediate management or outcomes.

safety_verdicts.content: The patient initially experienced a weird sensation around the lips.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact mentions the initial 'weird sensation' around the lips prior to swelling.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting an initial “weird sensation” around the lips removes a minor prodromal symptom that can support an evolving allergic reaction but is not essential to diagnosis or treatment decisions in this case. Clinical action (suspected anaphylaxis/ambulance) would remain the same.

safety_verdicts.content: Swelling started about 30 minutes after eating and is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not specify onset timing (~30 minutes after eating) or that swelling is localized to the upper lip.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing the onset timing (~30 minutes after eating) and precise location (upper lip) reduces specificity for an IgE-mediated food reaction and may impair downstream clinician interpretation of exposure-response chronology. While it likely wouldn’t change emergent care already initiated, it can cause resolution loss in documentation and handoff.

Dizziness can be a concerning systemic symptom in anaphylaxis (possible hypotension/impending collapse), and omitting it may understate severity for subsequent triage or handoff. Although emergency services were already advised, the missing red-flag symptom can still lead to less precise urgency assessment.

safety_verdicts.content: During consultation, the patient appeared to have breathing difficulties.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies an observed appearance of breathing difficulty during consultation; generated facts only document reported SOB and clinician concern, not an explicit observed breathing difficulty.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document observed breathing difficulty (as opposed to only patient-reported shortness of breath) may reduce the perceived acuity and objectivity of respiratory compromise in anaphylaxis. Even if disposition was already emergency escalation, this omission can affect handoff clarity and monitoring intensity.
